movie_characters.description: The fun-loving, mischievous, and brave hero, Veeru brought humor and heart to the film, creating an unforgettable bromance with Jai.
The calm, composed, and sharp-shooter partner to Veeru; Jai's cool demeanor and tragic end made him a timeless legend.
The ruthless, menacing dacoit whose iconic dialogue delivery ('Kitne aadmi the?') made him one of the most terrifying and memorable villains in Indian cinema history.
The dignified, stoic ex-police officer whose quest for justice after personal tragedy forms the emotional core of the story.
The spirited, talkative tonga driver whose feisty attitude and charm brought energy and humor, especially in her scenes with Veeru.
The silent, sorrowful widow who portrayed deep emotional strength and stoic endurance, offering a contrast to the action-packed story.
The bumbling, comic timber merchant whose small role became iconic for its hilarious dialogues and exaggerated mannerisms.
Gabbar Singh’s loyal henchman with minimal lines but maximum impact; his 'poochhne waale ka naam Sambha' dialogue became iconic.
Another memorable henchman of Gabbar, made famous by the chilling scene where Gabbar demands accountability ('Tera kya hoga Kaalia?').
The hilarious, bumbling British-style jailor whose satirical depiction of colonial officers became one of the film’s most famous comic reliefs.
The loyal servant of Thakur, whose heartfelt moments added emotional gravity to the storyline, especially during the flashback scenes.
Basanti’s talkative and practical aunt whose marriage discussions with Veeru created classic, humorous moments.
The wise and respected blind man of the village whose tragic loss highlighted the cruelty of Gabbar Singh and rallied the villagers' emotions.
